title: Bounding Speculative Execution of Atomic Regions to a Single Retry
problem: Hardware Transactional Memory implementations execute atomic regions speculatively with conflict detection, but retry conflicting executions multiple times before falling back to locks, creating uncertainty about the optimal retry strategy. The paper investigates how many retries are actually beneficial before the performance benefit is outweighed by retry overhead and conflict resolution costs.
motivation: Lock operations heavily dictate performance in parallel programs, and optimizing the retry policy for speculative execution can significantly improve parallel program performance.
method: The paper proposes bounding speculative execution to a single retry before falling back to mutual exclusion locks. This approach leverages hardware transactional memory conflict detection mechanisms to quickly identify conflicts and make deterministic fallback decisions, avoiding the overhead of repeated retry attempts.
key_novelty: The paper demonstrates that limiting HTM speculative execution to only a single retry before falling back to locks outperforms traditional multi-retry approaches, challenging the conventional wisdom about retry strategies in Hardware Transactional Memory systems.
contributions: Analysis showing single-retry strategy outperforms multi-retry HTM approaches
Practical policy for bounding speculative execution in atomic regions
Performance evaluation demonstrating speedup over baseline lock and multi-retry methods
Guidance for designing HTM retry policies in practical systems

metrics.speedup: versus multi-retry HTM and lock-based baselines

primary_theme: optimizing speculative execution retry strategy for transactional memory
